questions.text: User Technical Capability Assessment: Assess user ability to operate system: (1) Understanding of solar limitations (day/night, weather); (2) Load management skills (what appliances can run?); (3) Basic maintenance skills (cleaning panels); (4) Safety awareness (battery safety); (5) Digital literacy (for PAYG payments); (6) Troubleshooting ability; (7) Prior experience with solar.
questions.evidence_required: User assessment checklists, Training needs analysis, Digital literacy surveys
questions.africa_specific_notes: Users often overload systems (expect grid-like power). PAYG requires digital payment skills. Safety awareness low.

questions.text: Energy Literacy Assessment: Assess understanding of energy concepts: (1) Watts vs Watt-hours; (2) Battery capacity understanding; (3) Efficiency awareness (LED vs incandescent); (4) Cost of energy understanding; (5) Appliance rating awareness; (6) Energy saving behaviors; (7) Expectation management.
questions.evidence_required: Energy literacy survey results, Customer onboarding scripts
questions.africa_specific_notes: Misunderstanding 'Watts' leads to overloading. Users buy inefficient cheap appliances. Managing expectations is key to satisfaction.

questions.text: Business User Capability (Productive Use): For productive use of energy (PUE): (1) Business skills (cash flow to pay PAYG); (2) Appliance operation skills (milling, pumping, cooling); (3) Market access for products; (4) Financial management; (5) Technical maintenance of PUE equipment; (6) Business planning; (7) Risk management.
questions.evidence_required: Business capability assessment, PUE training records, Income verification
questions.africa_specific_notes: PUE (Productive Use of Energy) is a growth area. Users need business skills, not just power, to succeed and repay.

questions.text: User Training Program - Solar Home Systems: Describe user training: (1) Installation training (if self-install); (2) Operation training (dos and don'ts); (3) Payment training (how to pay via mobile money); (4) Maintenance training (cleaning); (5) Safety training; (6) Training materials (visual, local language); (7) Verification of understanding.
questions.evidence_required: Training guides, Agent training checklists, User sign-off sheets
questions.africa_specific_notes: Training must be at point of sale/installation. Visuals essential. Payment training critical for PAYG.

questions.text: Technician Training & Certification: Ensure technician competence: (1) Solar installation training (PV sizing, wiring, safety); (2) Troubleshooting & repair training; (3) Safety certification (working at heights, electrical); (4) Product-specific training; (5) Soft skills (customer interaction); (6) Certification (national curriculum?); (7) Refresher training.
questions.evidence_required: Training curriculum, Technician certificates, Safety training logs, Refresher schedules
questions.africa_specific_notes: Poor installation = #1 cause of failure. Local technicians need formal training. Safety often overlooked.

questions.text: Sales Agent Training: Ensure agents sell correctly: (1) Product capability training (don't oversell); (2) Financial terms training (explain PAYG clearly); (3) Assessment training (sizing system for user); (4) Ethics training; (5) Troubleshooting basics; (6) Mobile money training; (7) Ongoing coaching.
questions.evidence_required: Agent training manual, Ethics code, Product knowledge tests
questions.africa_specific_notes: Agents often oversell capabilities ('it can run a TV' when it can't). Financial terms explanation critical.

questions.text: Technical Support Infrastructure: Accessibility of support: (1) Call center availability (hours, languages); (2) Field technician network (coverage, response time); (3) Remote diagnostics capability; (4) Spare parts logistics; (5) Service centers (walk-in); (6) Self-help resources; (7) Escalation process.
questions.evidence_required: Support channel map, Technician coverage map, Spare parts inventory, SLA data
questions.africa_specific_notes: Remote diagnostics save truck rolls. Field technicians essential for hardware issues. Spare parts logistics is the bottleneck.

questions.text: Payment Support Services: Support for PAYG issues: (1) Payment troubleshooting (failed transactions); (2) Token entry support (unlocking system); (3) Account status queries; (4) Restructuring plans (for hardship); (5) Refund processing; (6) Mobile money agent liaison; (7) Grace period requests.
questions.evidence_required: Payment support scripts, Hardship policies, Refund logs
questions.africa_specific_notes: Payment issues = darkness. Users need immediate help. Hardship policies needed for shocks (drought, COVID).

questions.text: Product Adaptation from Feedback: Improving products for Africa: (1) Feedback loops (technicians -> engineering); (2) Product modifications (e.g., stronger cables, dust protection); (3) Software updates (PAYG logic); (4) User interface improvements; (5) Failure analysis integration; (6) Pilot testing of new features; (7) Local R&D.
questions.evidence_required: Product iteration logs, Field failure reports, R&D roadmaps
questions.africa_specific_notes: Products must evolve for African reality (e.g., rat-proof cables, tamper resistance). Feedback from field techs is gold.

questions.text: Local Capacity Building: Building long-term local skills: (1) Training local trainers; (2) Partnering with vocational schools; (3) Career paths for agents/techs; (4) Management training for local staff; (5) Gender inclusion in technical roles; (6) Knowledge transfer from expats; (7) Industry association participation.
questions.evidence_required: Capacity building programs, Partnership MOUs, Staff promotion records
questions.africa_specific_notes: Sustainable sector needs local experts. Vocational schools key partners. Women often excluded from technical roles.

questions.text: Regulatory & Institutional Capacity Building: Support for sector governance: (1) Regulator training (educating officials on DRE technologies); (2) Standard setting support (helping define quality standards); (3) Data sharing for planning (sharing usage data to help national planning); (4) Policy advocacy (constructive engagement on tariffs/subsidies); (5) Utility partnership (working with national utility, not just competing); (6) Association leadership (leading industry bodies).
questions.evidence_required: Training workshop records, Policy submission papers, Data sharing agreements
questions.africa_specific_notes: Regulators often unfamiliar with off-grid tech. Industry must help build their capacity.

questions.text: Spare Parts & Warranty Supply Chain: Availability of parts: (1) In-country inventory levels; (2) Last-mile distribution of parts; (3) Reverse logistics (collecting e-waste/faulty units); (4) Customs clearance efficiency; (5) Local sourcing (cables, mounts); (6) Inventory management systems; (7) Supply chain resilience.
questions.evidence_required: Inventory reports, Logistics contracts, Reverse logistics plan, Customs data
questions.africa_specific_notes: Spare parts often stuck in port. Last-mile distribution expensive. Reverse logistics critical for e-waste.

questions.text: Local Installation & Maintenance Ecosystem: Capacity of local partners: (1) Third-party installer network; (2) Independent repair shops; (3) Quality control of partners; (4) Standardized pricing for services; (5) Tool availability; (6) Partner training & certification; (7) Geographic coverage.
questions.evidence_required: Partner map, QC reports, Service pricing lists, Tool inventories
questions.africa_specific_notes: Companies can't employ everyone - need partner ecosystem. Independent repair shops can extend product life if trained.

scoring_notes: Layer 4 (Competence) for Energy in SSA: Technician training is the backbone of reliability. User training prevents misuse/overloading. Local supply chain for spare parts is the biggest operational challenge.
